paragraphs: Enterprise buyers in Public Sector, Insurance, Healthcare and Finance aren't buying an algorithm. They're buying certainty about their own data, and a model reached only through an API gives them nothing to see. Model Playground is where Lazarus AI's models become visible: buyers prompt them directly, run custom demos and assemble tools that drop into their real workflows. One room serves as the customer demo and the internal test bench.

Led as both lead designer and product manager, alongside engineering. The product is a flexible architecture rather than a fixed interface: people ask for the inputs and outputs they need, and the system reshapes around them. That one decision serves three audiences on one shared design system: sales tailoring each customer walkthrough, designers testing new patterns as the models change, and the on-premise Public Sector deployments built from it.

Regulated industries refuse the black box. Lazarus AI builds foundation models for insurance, healthcare, banking and government, where every answer has to be traceable, so its identity is built as the black box's opposite: legible, exact and accountable. It signals precision without raising its voice. The work speaks, and the marketing recedes.

The brand was built from the ground up on five pillars: Cool, Capable, Critical, Premium, Inevitable. Wireframe and dithered textures, contour data visuals with a single Neon Ember Orange accent, and strict monochrome, so colour carries weight when it appears. The website shows one key visual, one statement, obscured client logos and a single call to action. An atomic component library, down to the chamfered chip and a purpose-built icon set, keeps it sharp as it grows. It lands with enterprise buyers in Public Sector and Healthcare who value substance over spectacle.

Putting the right person in the right role means weighing skills, constraints, context and a hundred intangibles, and the people deciding can't hand that judgment to a black box. Talent Management backs their judgment up instead of replacing it. Built on ATLS, Lazarus AI's agentic platform, it ranks candidates against open roles and explains every match, so decisions move with confidence.

An on-prem deployment that scores the full pool against the customer's own methodology. The rationale shows at every level, from the dashboard down to a single result, with constraint toggles to refine the pool and side-by-side comparisons. In production it cut cycle times from months to minutes, without giving up accuracy or the human judgment that makes the call.

In the field, speed and certainty are the same requirement. Operators have to flag a hostile drone or confirm a platform meets the mission on the spot, and trust the answer enough to act on it. Whitelist puts that call in their hand. Built on ATLS, Lazarus AI's agentic platform, it draws on partnered drone research, production data and open-source intelligence, and returns a verdict with the reasoning behind it.

The prompting and analysis patterns from Model Playground carry into a mobile-first design, so operators move between phone in the field and desktop at base with nothing to relearn. Whitelist sets the standard for how every Lazarus AI product behaves in the field. It is in development and QA, heading into MVP testing with 50 users.

The feed isolates: posts go to a timeline, and community is a layer bolted on top. Chatter inverts it. Every post belongs to a group, rooms run live, and creators earn without leaving the room. A group-first social app for creators and their communities, launched on iPhone in July 2024 and announced by Davido.

Groups, Live Rooms and Stream let creators host real conversations and perform live, with the audience taking part instead of watching. RocketChats, paid messages that rise above the room, along with subscriptions and ticketed events, let creators earn without spending the community's trust. App, brand and system, from zero to launch, through years of iteration and testing.

Most DeFi lending floats: rates move with the pool. Jet Protocol fixed it. Fixed Rate puts lending on Solana into an open order book, where lenders and borrowers set rate and term as makers and takers, and autoroll carries a position past maturity. The mechanism is complex. The surface couldn't be.

A complete redesign of the platform: the variable-rate lending experience reworked, and new products launched beside it, fixed-term markets and an Orca LP integration for borrowing against wallet collateral. The interface holds several trading modes at once without the flows collapsing into complexity. The brand was tightened in the same pass to say plainly what the protocol offers: precision, accessibility and reliability. It relaunched as Fixed Rate in June 2023.

Novart lets collectors borrow against their art. A loan against a collection used to mean one long application, filled in before anyone knew whether it would be approved. Novart turns it into two quick checks, a short form and a dashboard, and sits between lender and borrower from request to decision.

Two gates come first, location and minimum collateral value, and screen out likely denials before anyone invests time. A short form follows, then a dashboard: action items for each artwork, the status of every offer, a line to lenders and admins, and review, accept or decline. A heavy, front-loaded process becomes steps a person can pick up and put down.

Professional market data has always sat behind a paywall and a desk. The Terminal removes both. Data, analysis, news and education share one surface for everyday investors, with tiers that scale from learner to active trader. Urvin Finance built it for its community, and about 2,000 backers on Wefunder funded it.

News and Education were led here, along with the early data and chart explorations, with support on communities, authentication and data. Education lives inside the Terminal and free to everyone on a companion site built on Webflow, with writing, audio and video. Where user data was thin, design leaned on sibling products like News and tested with Alpha and Beta users; elsewhere, prototyping and testing with Sprig kept user needs central.

Understanding real estate risk means moving from a national view down to a single property without losing the data that matters. CoreLogic's Discovery Center in Texas makes that move physical: executives explore their portfolios across churn, hazards and liens on a 6×3 video wall, guided by Cora, a digital person who acts as their chief of staff. Designed and built at Soul Machines.

The video wall is driven from a touch table in the Discovery Center, with a desktop version for executives working remotely. Cora works the filters and explains what is on screen, and her dialogue was designed with the interface so each reinforces the other.

Bakers used to phone Nestlé's customer line with their questions. Now Ruth answers them. A digital person built by Soul Machines, she walks people at home through the perfect Toll House chocolate chip cookie in real time, finds recipes from what's already in the cupboard, and lets them shop for next time. A customer line, given a face. She debuted in February 2021.

Less than 1% of the furniture made by leading brands is designed by Black designers. HUE+MAN answers that with a global design competition and a travelling installation that open resources and access to BIPOC creatives. It's a collaboration between Kevin Jones's Joba Studio and USM, the Swiss maker whose modular furniture has been in production for over fifty years. It began in 2020.

“Hue is an old term for culture,” Jones explains, and HUE+MAN stands for Culture + Humanity. Shown at Design Miami, the installation puts viewers inside that idea: design as expression and empowerment, and a way to start difficult conversations.
